answer: Random-Committee Admission Draw. Each epoch, an agent must submit a fresh commitment to a random seed derived from a public beacon, then a small random committee admits a bounded quota of identities. An attacker cannot precompute favorable seeds, so mass registrations face a rising summit of repeated failed draws. Admission also requires proof of a distinct communication jetty to a random vertex chosen after commitment, forcing real per-identity infrastructure. Each surviving identity costs fresh setup plus failed-draw overhead, making bulk sybils linearly expensive.
